E-2-1 has a maximum design pressure of 10.3 barg (150 psig) per ASME or 16.0 barg (232 psig) per PED. FV-2-1's limits are per ASME B16.34 (e.g., up to 104 bar / 1500 psig with ENVIRO-SEAL Graphite ULF packing) depending on class and trim. BV-2-1 and BV-3-1 have pressure/temperature ratings by class (e.g., Class 150 from 19.8 bar down to 10.2 bar at 300 °C; Class 300 up to about 51.8 bar) and by seat material, with soft seats dropping to 0 bar at elevated temperatures (e.g., virgin PTFE 0 bar at about 228 °C, reinforced PTFE 0 bar at about 229 °C, PEEK 0 bar at about 300 °C). The lowest maximum allowable pressure on the path is therefore 0 bar, applying to the ball valves BV-2-1 and BV-3-1 when fitted with soft seat materials at their limiting temperatures; among the more typical ratings, E-2-1's 10.3 barg is the lowest fixed design pressure.

MATCH (p:PlantItem {tag:'P-7-2'})-[:line_to]->(it:PlantItem)

final.answer: The items receiving flow directly from P-25-1 are the ball valves BV-25-1 and BV-25-3. Their datasheets (pages 6-7) do not state a single maximum fluid temperature; instead they give pressure/temperature rating tables (ASME B16.34, temperatures tabulated from -30 °C to 300 °C) and maximum seat temperature limits by seat material, ranging from 80 °C (Delrin) up to 315 °C (PEEK or metal seats). Since both valves carry the same datasheet data, neither has a uniquely lowest maximum — they are equal.

final.answer: The valve operated by TIC-27-2 is TV-27-2, and the item directly upstream of BV-24-1 is heat exchanger E-24-1. E-24-1's datasheet gives a maximum design temperature of 177 °C (350 °F) under the ASME code (180 °C / 356 °F under PED). TV-27-2's datasheet does not state which seat material this specific valve has, so its fluid-temperature limit cannot be pinned to one value: it ranges from 80 °C (180 °F) for Delrin seats and 90 °C (200 °F) for UHMWPE seats, up to 230–260 °C for PTFE/Polyfill seats and 315 °C (600 °F) for PEEK or metal seats. Therefore, which of the two has the lowest maximum fluid temperature depends on TV-27-2's seat material: with Delrin or UHMWPE seats the valve (80–90 °C) is lower than the exchanger (177 °C), but with any other seat material the exchanger (177 °C) is the lower of the two.

Comparing datasheet ratings, E-27-1 has by far the lowest maximum allowable pressure: its Alfa Laval M3 datasheet gives 10.3 barg (150 psig) under the ASME code, or 16.0 barg (232 psig) under the PED code. The check valve CHV-27-1's datasheet (Swagelok C/CA/CH/CP/CPA series) does not identify the specific series/size, but even its lowest stated ratings (e.g. 200 psig max back pressure for the 8C/12C/16C fixed series) exceed the exchanger's ASME rating, with an overall maximum of up to 6000 psig (413 bar) for CH4/CH8. So E-27-1 has the lowest maximum allowable pressure, at 10.3 barg (150 psig) ASME or 16.0 barg (232 psig) PED, versus up to 6000 psig (413 bar) for CHV-27-1.

# Maximum Allowable Pressure

The datasheet does not give one single maximum pressure number. The maximum inlet pressure depends on the pressure rating class of your valve's body and connection style, and the whole assembly (packing, body material, trim) must never exceed its own pressure/temperature rating.

**Pressure ratings for the valve body (steel valve body, raised-face), depending on the product variant [p. 5]:**
- PN16 (ET, EAT, ETR variants)
- PN25 (EAT, ETR variants)
- PN40 (ET, EAT variants)
- PN63 (EAT, ETR variants)
- PN100 (ET, ETR variants)

**Maximum inlet pressures and temperatures, per connection type [p. 3, Table 1]:**
- Steel and stainless steel bodies, flanged: consistent with CL150, 300 and 600 per ASME B16.34
- Steel and stainless steel bodies, screwed or welding: consistent with flanged CL600 per ASME B16.34
- Cast iron bodies, flanged: consistent with CL125B or 250B per ASME B16.1

These are "unless limited by maximum pressure drop or material temperature capabilities" [p. 3]. The Ordering Information section adds that the inlet pressure and temperature "must always be limited by the applicable ASME pressure/temperature rating" [p. 32].

**Limits for the packing system (Table 2, ENVIRO-SEAL Packing System Specifications, p. 5):**
- ENVIRO-SEAL Graphite ULF packing: maximum pressure 1500 psig / 104 bar, at a temperature up to 316 °C / 600 °F
- ENVIRO-SEAL PTFE and Duplex packing: maximum temperature 232 °C / 450 °F (no separate pressure limit is given for this packing in the facts)

- "The pressure or temperature limits in this bulletin and any applicable code limitations, should not be exceeded" [p. 3, 4, 5]
- "Do not exceed the maximum pressure and temperature for the pressure rating of the body material used, even though the trims shown may have higher capabilities" (notes on Figures 13, 14 and 15, p. 18, 19, 26)

Note: "PN" and "CL" are pressure class ratings — they tell you which pressure/temperature table of the referenced standard (ASME B16.34 or B16.1) applies to your valve; the actual maximum pressure depends on the temperature too.

**Related limits (pressure drop, not inlet pressure):** The maximum allowable pressure drop must not exceed the lowest value indicated for the combination of materials selected [p. 32]; the drop limits are shown in Figures 13, 14 and 15 (charts of fluid/liquid temperature versus pressure drop in bar/psi, p. 18–19 and 26). For example, trims 4 and 29 (and trim 85) may be used up to 99 bar / 1440 psi with clean dry gas, but only up to 21 bar / 300 psi for other process fluids [p. 18, 26].

A note on page 3 warns: the pressure or temperature limits in the bulletin and any applicable code limitations should not be exceeded.

final.answer: The path is E-13-2 → P-13-2 → TV-13-2 → P-22-1 → CHV-22-1 → PV-22-1 → P-22-2. Values from the datasheets: E-13-2 (Alfa Laval M3): max design pressure 10.3 barg (150 psig) per ASME code, or 16.0 barg per PED code, frame FG. P-13-2, P-22-1 and P-22-2 (Gorman-Rupp pumps, same datasheet): max operating pressure 250 psi (1723 kPa, up to 100 °F); max casing pressure 266 psi (1834 kPa). TV-13-2 (Fisher ET): no single numeric maximum pressure is stated; the limit depends on the pressure class (PN16–PN100 / CL150–CL600 per ASME B16.34) and temperature. CHV-22-1 (Swagelok check valve): no single number; depends on variant and temperature (e.g. CH4/CH8 316 SS up to 6000 psig / 413 bar at ≤100 °F; 12C/16C 2000 psig / 137 bar). PV-22-1 (Flowserve Worcester ball valve): no single number; given by the pressure/temperature chart (e.g. Class 150 Group 1.2: 19.4 bar at 50 °C), with seat material limits possibly lower. The item with the lowest maximum allowable pressure is E-13-2, at 10.3 barg (150 psig) under the ASME code (16.0 barg under PED), which is lower than the pumps' 250 psi (~17.2 bar) and the valve ratings.

# Maximum allowable pressure

The maximum allowable pressure depends on which valve variant you have, the temperature, and the material — there is no single number. The highest rating given is **6000 psig (413 bar)** for the CH4 and CH8 check valves in 316 stainless steel, at 10°F (−12°C) to 100°F (37°C) [p. 3]. Note: a footnote says this rating may be limited by the end connection — see the Dimensions table on page 12.

**Working pressure (highest safe operating pressure) by variant, 316 SS valves** — see the "Pressure-Temperature Ratings" tables on page 3:

- **CH4 / CH8:** 6000 psig (413 bar) at 10°F (−12°C) to 100°F (37°C); 5160 psig (355 bar) at 200°F (93°C); 4910 psig (338 bar) at 250°F (121°C); 4660 psig (321 bar) at 300°F (148°C); 4280 psig (294 bar) at 400°F (204°C) [p. 3]

- **12C / 16C:** 2000 psig (137 bar) at −10°F (−23°C) to 100°F (37°C), decreasing to 1450 psig (99.9 bar) at 375°F (190°C) [p. 3]

A footnote on the C/CA/CP/CPA table warns: for 2C and 4C valves, and 6C/8C valves with cracking pressures below 50 psi (3.5 bar), an optional inlet gasket is available to reduce the risk of the O-ring (the soft seal inside) being dislodged in systems with pressure surges, shock, or pulses — see page 14 [p. 3].

**Related limits, in case "maximum pressure" means something else for you:**

- **Maximum back pressure** (the pressure the valve can hold against on its outlet side) — "Technical Data" table 1, page 3, all at 70°F (20°C):
  - CH8 (fixed cracking pressure): 6000 psig (413 bar), footnote: may be limited by the end connection — see Dimensions, page 12 [p. 3]
  - 4CP, 8CP, 8CPA, CA, 4CPA: 3000 psig (206 bar) [p. 3]
  - 2C: 1000 psig (68.9 bar), except when the cracking pressure is 25 psi (1.8 bar), then 3000 psig (206 bar) [p. 3]
  - 12C / 16C: 200 psig (13.7 bar) [p. 3]

- **Pressure rating by end connection** (CH Series, at 100°F / 37°C) — "Dimensions" table, page 12: e.g. Female ISO 1/2 in.: 5100 psig (351 bar); Male ISO 3/4 in. or 1 in.: 5000 psig (344 bar); Swagelok tube fitting 1/8–3/8 in.: 6000 psig (413 bar) [p. 12]

- **ECE R110-type-approved valves** (a European gas-vehicle approval): pressure rating within the range 3770 psig (260 bar) [p. 14]

For completeness: "cracking pressure" (the pressure at which the valve opens) is a separate parameter, with nominal values from 1/3 psi (0.03 bar) up to 25 psi (1.8 bar) depending on variant [pp. 3–4].
